title: APO Turkey Roulades with Spinach and Parmesan Gravy
description: Thin turkey breast rolls steam around a soft spinach filling and are served with extra Parmesan gravy.
equipment: Anova Precision Oven Gen 1 with food probe, bottom drip pan and middle wire rack

ingredients.name: plain skinless turkey breast cutlets
ingredients.note: Two wide pieces, no injected brine.

ingredients.name: low-sodium turkey broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water without a vegetable seasoning blend. Reserve three quarters of the measured broth for the gravy.

steps.title: Preheat the APO
steps.text: Fill the water tank and install the bottom drip pan. Preheat to 300°F with sous vide mode off, 80% steam, rear element on, top and bottom elements off. Set the food probe target to 165°F.

steps.title: Soften the spinach
steps.text: Steam {spinach} and {garlic} with a splash of {broth} in the covered HexClad over medium heat for 2–3 minutes. Cool just enough to handle, press out excess liquid and mince to a soft paste.

steps.title: Thin the cutlets
steps.text: Pound {turkey} gently between parchment sheets to about 1/4 inch thick using a meat mallet.

steps.title: Roll around the filling
steps.text: Spread a thin layer of spinach over each cutlet, leaving a small border. Roll from a short end and secure with kitchen twine; keep each finished roll no thicker than 1 1/2 inches.

steps.title: Insert the probe
steps.text: Lay the rolls seam down in a small covered oven dish with just enough {broth} to moisten the bottom, reserving three quarters for gravy. Insert the probe from one end into the center of the thickest filling.

steps.title: Steam the roulades
steps.text: Cook covered on the middle rack for 20–40 minutes. Check the center of the spinach and the thickest turkey seam in each roll with a clean thermometer. Continue until both places reach 165°F in every roll.

steps.title: Rest the rolls
steps.text: Rest the turkey covered in its juices for 5 minutes, then remove all twine.

steps.title: Start the gravy
steps.text: Meanwhile bring the reserved {broth} and {zest} to a simmer in the HexClad for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Make the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and keep it bubbling gently for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Melt the Parmesan
steps.text: Turn off the heat and whisk in {cheese} until smooth.

steps.title: Serve the pinwheels
steps.text: Slice each roulade across the spiral. Spoon the gravy over and between the pinwheels, with extra around each serving.

notes: Make ahead: Make the spinach filling a day ahead and refrigerate. Roll the turkey just before cooking. Option A uses lemon zest. For gentler Option B, omit it. For a dairy-free version, replace Parmesan with finely chopped parsley stirred into the finished gravy. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Chill and freeze individual sliced rolls with gravy for up to 2 months to protect the thin turkey layers. Fridge reheat: Place one portion and its sauce in a shallow covered dish. Install the APO bottom drip pan and preheat to 325°F, sous vide mode off, 60% steam, rear element on, top and bottom off. Insert the probe in the coldest center and set it to 165°F. Start checking after 12 minutes and heat to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw a single portion in the refrigerator overnight, then use the fridge reheating method. Stir the sauce until smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 204 kcal, 36.7 g protein, 5.4 g total carbohydrate, 3.0 g fat, 0.5 g fiber, 264 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
